##### Summary

Ansible-lint and yamllint always complain about the missing role name and namespace definitition in `./meta/main.yml`.
Also the min_ansible_version is interpreted as a float number instead of a string - another complaint.
other changes are a consistent order of:

1. documentation, then
2. parameter

The comments are now intended as the text/parameters they belong to.
Since `./meta/main.yml` is a yaml file, the file now starts with `---` as well.

Fixes #84150

##### ISSUE TYPE

- Feature Pull Request

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

If you run `ansible-galaxy role init example.test` , then enter the role and run `yamllint .` and `ansible-lint .`, the 
output will cover a number of violations regarding

* comment indentation
* missing yaml document headers
* minimum ansible version
* ~~missing field `namespace`~~
* ~~missing field `role_name`~~

in addition (but ignored in this PR)

* Author name should be changed
* License should be chosen.
* Company should be changed

This PR is trying to fix at least the easy fixable violations and reduce the starting work when creating a new role.

issue_context.title: Linting compatible `/meta/main.yml` file
issue_context.body:
### Summary

The problem I am trying to address is  that the file `./meta/main.yml` not per se is wrong, but considering common linters like `ansible-lint` and `yamllint` the file could be better formatted and reduce the amount of work required to create new rules.

Currently running `ansible-galaxy role init ....` creates a file that is always incompatible with at least `ansible-lint` and `yamllint` and triggers multiple default rules. This either requires to adjust the content of the file or create exceptions in linting for this particular file.

My current workaround is an Ansible role to create new roles and perform the required changes during creation.
But I think `ansible-galaxy` could do better and the output pass more linting rules of both linters.

### Issue Type

Feature Idea

### Component Name

ansible-galaxy

### Additional Information

I'd like to propose as in GitHub Issue #82394 (which has been closed as non-bug) to make minor adjustments to `./meta/main.yml` to pass the `ansible-lint` and `yamllint` default linting rules by

* making the comment positions consistent.
   Some comments for fields are placed before the actual field, some are placed behind the field. This is inconsistent and a bit confusing every time even I look at it.
* adding fields for role name and namespace.
   Adding the field `role_name` and `namespace` based on the role name from the `ansible-galaxy`-command.
* Limit the line length to pass yamllint in its default configuration.
   The changes are simply adjusting linebreaks.
* Format the field `min_ansible_version` as string instead as float within the file. The default value is `2.1` which then would be handled as a floating point. `Ansible-lint` suggests `"2.1"`, although I cannot find a reason for this in the documentation.
   This is required to be adjusted to pass any `ansible-lint` run when this is used for linting.

The suggested [PR 84146 ](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/84146/) passes `yamllint` and `ansible-lint` with their default configuration.
I'd appreciate comments or improvements regarding the fields `role_name` and `namespace`. There are changes involving the python script creating the actual file and I most likely have broken some rules for these minor changes there to get the correct values into the output file.

### Code of Conduct

- [X] I agree to follow the Ansible Code of Conduct

Hi!

Thanks very much for your submission to Ansible.  It means a lot to us that you've taken time to contribute.

Unfortunately, we're not sure if we want this feature in the program, and I don't want this to seem confrontational.
Our reasons for this are:

* `ansible-lint` enforces stricter rules than those required or supported by `ansible-core`.
* The default templates are intended as a starting point - a simple example that works with `ansible-core` without modification, but they are expected to be edited to add tags, dependencies, etc.
* There are `ansible-lint` violations across multiple files in the default templates, so focusing only on `meta/main.yml` seems arbitrary. Fixing issues piecemeal like this would introduce unnecessary churn for the templates.
* Fixing all violations won't prevent future divergence, as ansible-lint adds rules independently of `ansible-core`.
* Using a custom role skeleton can streamline role creation by aligning with the specific lint rules your project follows, and negate the need to manually edit the initialized roles.

However, we're absolutely always up for discussion.
Because this project is very active, we're unlikely to see comments made on closed tickets and we lock them after some time.
If you or anyone else has any further questions, please let us know by using any of the communication methods listed in the page below:

* <https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/community/communication.html>

In the future, sometimes starting a discussion on the development list prior to implementing
a feature can make getting things included a little easier, but it's not always necessary.

Thank you once again for this and your interest in Ansible!
Hi @s-hertel, thanks for you response. Event though this issue has been closed, I'd like to comment to your explanation.

> * There are `ansible-lint` violations across multiple files in the default templates, so focusing only on `meta/main.yml` seems arbitrary. Fixing issues piecemeal like this would introduce unnecessary churn for the templates.

Creating a blank role with `ansible-galaxy role init $namespace.rolename` creates a role that only violates `yamllint`  (1.35.1) and `ansible-lint` (24.9.2) on in `./meta/main.yml`.
Can you elaborate which other linting issues you referring to? I don't seem to be able to re-create the situation you are describing. I'd really like to be aware of the other issues, which I have not seen.

Would a issue/PR get more likely accepted if it contained all the other issues as well?

> * Fixing all violations won't prevent future divergence, as ansible-lint adds rules independently of `ansible-core`.
 
Agree. Does this prevent fixing any number of issues (like leading `---` in the first line)?

Following your argumentation fixing all linting issue does not seem to make sense, but I consider the current default template still a bit under what could be done to provide a slightly better experience. So I am aiming for that.

Thanks and keep up the work.
